column1: # premise: Frozen is picked and chilled fast; read the bag: organic, one ingredient, loose pieces.

column5: Bag says "wild"; ingredients list blueberries alone.
column6: Wild lowbush stands are unplanted and the berries are marketed as "wild"; about 98-99% of the crop is frozen. Lowbush averaged higher in anthocyanins in a 2001 study, while a 2012 study found some highbush cultivars overlapping or above.

column5: No "wild" on the bag means planted highbush; ingredients blueberries alone.
column6: Cultivated highbush is a different plant from lowbush and the composition gap is not uniform: one study found several highbush varieties above its single lowbush sample in anthocyanidins.

column5: Berries loose and individually frozen; ingredients strawberries alone.
column6: Frozen strawberries are individually quick frozen so pieces separate, and one UC Davis comparison found frozen produce comparable to fresh in measured vitamins.

column5: Whole berries, loose in the bag; ingredients raspberries alone.
column6: Extension guides tray-freeze firm, well-colored raspberries so pieces stay loose; in one 12-month study at -20 C, vitamin C fell 33-55%.

column5: Plump glossy berries loose in the bag; ingredients blackberries alone.
column6: Extension guides pick firm, plump, glossy ripe berries and tray-pack them so the pieces remain loose.

column5: Cherries loose, deep dark color; ingredients cherries alone, no sugar.
column6: Cherries freeze individually on a tray, dark color is the best indication of good flavor, and unsweetened frozen cherries come out softer once thawed.

column5: Ingredients name each berry, such as strawberry and blueberry; no sugar or juice.
column6: Ingredients are listed in descending order of weight, so an added sweetener shows up as its own named line.

column5: Chunks loose, not fused; ingredients mango alone, no sugar line.
column6: Fresh mangoes are usually picked green for shipping; the freezing guide calls for firm ripe fruit, unsweetened tray pack.

column5: Ingredients name mango, pineapple or papaya; no sugar, syrup or juice.
column6: Ingredients are listed in descending order of weight, so the order of the list shows what the bag holds most of.

column5: Organic seal on the bag; ingredients papaya alone.
column6: Papaya is on the Non-GMO Project high-risk crop list, and organic standards prohibit excluded methods, which is why the seal decides it.

column5: Ingredients name acai alone; skip packs listing sweeteners before the fruit.
column6: One study describes frozen pulp as acai berry and water only, with anthocyanins down 21% after 15 days at -18 C.

column5: Bright round peas, loose in the bag; ingredients peas alone.
column6: Fresh peas start turning sugar to starch within hours of harvest, while processors aim to chill peas within about three hours of picking.

column5: Kernels loose, not one block; ingredients corn alone, organic seal.
column6: Sweet corn can lose about a third of its sugar within 24 hours at room temperature, and corn is on the Non-GMO Project high-risk list, which is why the organic seal matters.

column5: Ingredients spinach alone; skip creamed bags listing cream or starch.
column6: One UC Davis comparison found spinach lower in beta-carotene when frozen, while overall vitamin content of frozen produce was comparable to fresh.

column5: Chopped leaves loose, not one solid block; ingredients name the greens only.
column6: Tray-frozen greens separate more easily, while greens frozen as a solid block must be partly thawed before heating; guides pick young, tender leaves.

column5: Dark green compact florets, no yellow buds; ingredients broccoli alone.
column6: Extension guides pick bright green heads with compact dark green buds and reject yellowing ones; blanching before freezing slows enzyme activity.

column5: Creamy white florets, no grey or brown; ingredients cauliflower alone.
column6: Extension guides pick white or creamy-white firm heads and avoid discoloration; blanching brightens color and slows vitamin loss.

column5: Riced cauliflower bag: ingredients say cauliflower alone, no starch or seasoning.
column6: Ingredients are listed in descending order of weight, so a starch or seasoning line means it is a real part of the bag.

column5: Pieces separate, not a frozen clump; ingredients carrots alone, organic seal.
column6: Carrots measured lower in beta-carotene frozen than fresh in one UC Davis comparison, and blanching is a standard step before freezing.

column5: Slim crisp-looking pods, ingredients green beans alone, no white frost.
column6: Green beans are blanched before freezing to inactivate enzymes, and over-blanching can harm quality; one UC Davis comparison found no significant beta-carotene difference.

column5: Small tight sprouts; ingredients Brussels sprouts alone, no loose leaves.
column6: Extension guides pick green, firm, compact heads and sort them by size; small, firm, compact sprouts are the best choice.

column5: Beans or pods loose in the bag; ingredients edamame alone, organic seal.
column6: Vegetable soybean is perishable and is sold fresh or frozen, and soy is on the Non-GMO Project high-risk crop list, which is why the organic seal matters.

column5: Skip bags with a sauce packet; ingredients name vegetables only.
column6: A survey of retail frozen vegetable blends found clumping and frostbite defects, so loose pieces and no frost are the shelf check.

column5: Ingredients name peas, carrots, corn and green beans; bag tips loose, not a block.
column6: Thawed and refrozen vegetables clump together with freezer-burn frost, which is why a solid block is the sign to skip.

column5: Slices separate; ingredients squash or zucchini alone, organic seal.
column6: Zucchini and yellow summer squash are on the Non-GMO Project high-risk crop list, and organic standards prohibit excluded methods.

column5: Orange cubes loose; ingredients squash alone, no butter or brown sugar.
column6: Winter squash cubes freeze in a single layer on trays and go straight into recipes; guides pick firm, mature squash with a hard rind.

column2: Sauced, buttered or seasoned veg bags
column5: Skip bags with butter, cream, cheese, sauce or seasoning in the ingredients.
column6: Ingredients are listed in descending order of weight, so a sauce word high on the list means more sauce than vegetable.

column5: Skip bags listing sugar, syrup or juice concentrate; fruit should be the whole list.
column6: Ingredients are listed in descending order of weight, so sugar near the top outweighs the fruit.
